summary: Feed s120_double to IDS is degraded: 21.8% of TCP sessions are one-way (exceeds 10% threshold) and tool port is overloaded by 35% bursts (1.35 Gbps vs 1 Gbps). IDS stateful detection is impaired and bursts will cause drops at the IDS NIC.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is not aggregating both directions of a flow to the same IDS tool port. 27 of 124 TCP sessions (21.8%) show only one direction, typical of asymmetric routing combined with single-direction SPAN/TAP forwarding or per-direction load-balancing that hashes client->server and server->client to different tools.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires both directions (needs_both_directions=true) for TCP reassembly, stream tracking and signature matching. With one side missing, sessions stay half-open, state tables fill, and attacks that span request/response or require server response verification are missed - high false-negative risk.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both directions of each flow to the same IDS port using a bidirectional 5-tuple hash on the packet broker so the IDS sees complete sessions for stateful inspection.

findings.root_cause: Microbursts exceed the IDS 1 Gbps port capacity. Peak measured 1.35 Gbps in 1ms intervals (135% of capacity, 4 overloaded intervals). Even though broker shows no drops, the tool NIC itself will drop during bursts.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS with 1 Gbps port cannot ingest 1.35 Gbps bursts; packets are dropped at ingress before analysis. With needs_full_payload=true, any loss breaks detection, causes missed alerts and incomplete forensic evidence.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2+ IDS ports/instances with bidirectional-aware hashing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and preserve both directions per flow while eliminating burst drops.
